preference_scope: Clear collar/lapel readability preference; moderate overall visual preference because most whole-garment features are shared.

whole_garment_assessment.relative_shape_difference: No substantial body, sleeve, waist or ornament-placement advantage is visible between A and B.
recognized_identity: Long outward-falling sleeves and open front
Pale piping, waist and cuff buckles, shoulder tabs
Asymmetric shield emblems and two draped chains
shared_deviations: Smoother, more schematic torso and sleeve shaping than the tailored source
Simplified shield emblems instead of the ornate fleur-de-lis-like source marks
Missing or not visibly represented hanging pendant cluster and prominent rear shoulder ornament
Bright silver-gray waist and cuff bands obscure dark-strap versus silver-hardware separation
Uniform cylindrical cuffs and limited pale inner/under-cuff strip
Limited local cloth folds, compression and construction depth

preference_reasons: B has a coherent outer trim path through collar point, notch and long lapel.
A shows separated, doubled-looking diagonal trim fragments and small ambiguous pointed layers in front, oblique and side views.
B's simpler neck-to-lapel silhouette more clearly communicates the source's collar-and-revers organization.

A: Fragmented collar piping and competing small diagonal trim paths
All shared substantial fidelity limitations remain
B: Broad planar upper lapels and abrupt upper tonal transition
Shelf-like outward rear collar lip with a visible dark interval below its edge
Neck-to-lapel roll and connection remain insufficiently persuasive
All shared substantial fidelity limitations remain

shared_visible_artifacts: Bright crescent/slit near the upper sleeve behind the lapel and pinched-looking side marks; underlying cause uncertain
A few tiny shoulder/upper-sleeve bright specks; not treated as proven holes or intersections
tradeoff_that_could_reverse_preference: B improves outline continuity but replaces A's more upright nape band and small pointed layers with broader, flatter planes and an outward collar lip. Prioritizing the upright nape and separated layers could reverse a local collar preference; it does not reverse the overall preference against the complete supplied source.
uncertainties: Concept-sheet cameras and lighting are unregistered with the candidate renders.
Proportional and material observations are visual impressions, not calibrated errors.
Small slits and separations cannot be diagnosed as specific construction defects from these images alone.
Render grain is not treated as garment texture or mesh damage.
